description.purpose: Composite agent: one hive that carries session-keeper@2.0.2, collector@2.0.6, dispatcher@1.0.0 and summarizer@2.0.0 as sub-units plus an llm brain slot, with every internal edge pre-wired -- the stamp promotion, the seam into the brain, the dispatcher lanes, the loopback with restore_ttl and its iteration bound, the close path, the write fan-out and the system.handover return. The topology the Egon rollout wired by hand, as one add_nodes.
description.use_when: Whenever a colony needs a conversational agent that remembers its own session: a chat surface, a phone line, an operator console. Instantiate via add_nodes AND wire the four ports via add_edges IN THE SAME MUTATION - the composite is edge-connected from apply on (no island dance). Instantiation needs ctx.model (a RESOLVED literal, K-H2 lane B).
description.not_in_scope: No tool cells - the tool set is the per-agent choice and its lanes are wired per instance on hop.tool_name. No memory hive, no surface proxy, no drain cell, no persona: the write target, the recall port, the reply sink and where errors land are all the parent tree's decision.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the composite's own path (`params.ports` is empty since GH #228; an edge naming ./session-keeper, ./collector, ./dispatcher, ./summarizer, ./brain or ./errors is refused with hive_port_boundary), and what a caller wants rides on hop.route -- the door edges in here decide which cell that means. Ingress: that path, lane in_turn (the parent edge MUST promote the channel identity to context.channel, otherwise every chat lands on the channel 'default'). Reply exit: the same path on hop.route=='answer' (two sorts, told apart by hop.round_capped). Write exit: the same path on hop.route=='write' (the closed session as one batch; the target is the parent's choice), and OPTIONALLY the same path on hop.route=='turn_write' with params.turn_write set - the same batch after every stored turn, into the SAME target, so a memory behind it is fresh per turn and the close batch stays its safety net. Error drain: the same path on hop.route=='error' (MUST be wired). Per instance: the same path on hop.route=='tool' && hop.tool_name=='<name>' out to each tool cell, and every tool cell back into that same path with route in_tool. Optional: the recall / in_bundle pair for a memory hive, in_sweep, and the two operator lanes of the context window, in_prune and in_round_sweep. in_prune is PAIRED (since 3.0.6): it answers unconditionally -- with what it cut or with a zero report saying nothing was eligible -- on hop.route=='prune', and required_drains refuses a mutation that wires the ingress without a plain subscription to the report. The two tools the composite serves ITSELF are wired as a loop at that same path -- the tool lane back into the composite with the lane set: hop.tool_name=='memory_recall' -> in_memory_call, hop.tool_name=='thread_recall' -> in_thread_call (the latter since 3.0.1; without it every stub the collector's curator leaves points at a tool nobody can reach). The sub-units in here are sealed hives of their own, and for a caller that changes nothing: they are INTERIOR to this composite, which is sealed too, so an endpoint naming one of them -- or reaching past it, as in ./session-keeper/stamp or ./collector/assemble -- is refused with hive_port_boundary all the same. Which cell inside picks a message up is decided by the in_ lane the edge sets, by the door edges in here, and that is what lets the inside of a sub-unit change without touching a caller.
